title: Microsoft Purview DLP: restrict access to Fabric semantic models and lakehouses
summary: The briefing's access restrictions, opt-in default, licensing and asset-based billing are supported by Microsoft documentation and the supplied notice. Minor corrections should complete the portal route, cite its opening navigation and report the PowerShell reference's narrower capacity wording.

claims.claim: The roadmap adds a restrict access action for Fabric semantic models.
claims.quote: DLP restrict access action allows you to block access to guest users or all users depending on what labels or sensitive information types matches your semantic models or lakehouses.

claims.claim: The roadmap adds a restrict access action for Fabric lakehouses.
claims.quote: Your organization can now control who can access your data depending on the sensitive information detected in Fabric semantic models and lakehouses.

claims.quote: DLP evaluation of the semantic model doesn't occur if either of the following is true: An account using service principal authentication initiates the event (publish, republish, on-demand refresh, scheduled refresh).

claims.claim: The Fabric DLP configuration page names no licence for users whose access is restricted.
claims.quote: Searched: Fabric DLP restricted users licensing configuration admin E5 Purview capacities; opened Fabric DLP configuration and overview. The configuration page's licence list is explicitly for the admin account, not restricted users.

claims.claim: Mixed licensing reflects the documented admin entitlement and consumption billing.
claims.quote: The pay-as-you-go billing model builds on the per-user licensing model. The two are complementary, not mutually exclusive.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Fabric DLP evaluation workloads affect capacity consumption.
claims.quote: DLP evaluation workloads impact capacity consumption.

claims.claim: Microsoft Fabric DLP is covered by Purview pay-as-you-go asset billing.
claims.quote: | Azure | Fabric | Supported item types | Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention |

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go consumption is billed through Azure.
claims.quote: The billing mechanisms are Azure based, so you must associate your Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.

claims.claim: An asset is charged for each day that a policy covers it.
claims.quote: You're charged for each day that a policy covers an asset.

claims.claim: An asset in an in-scope location counts even when it does not match policy conditions.
claims.quote: The asset doesn't have to match a policy's conditions to be counted, it just has to be in a location that's in the scope of a policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft's example of five covered workspaces out of ten, each with 50 assets, yields an asset count of 250.
claims.quote: A tenant has 10 Fabric workspaces, each with 50 assets. The policy only applies to five of these Fabric workspaces. The asset count for this policy is 250.

claims.claim: The cited Fabric DLP and Purview billing-model pages quote no numerical rate for this action.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Fabric DLP restrict access pricing additional action charge asset per day; read Fabric DLP overview, configuration and Purview billing models in full. They describe entitlement, consumption and asset counting, but do not quote a numerical rate for the action.

claims.claim: A charge specific to restrict access beyond asset counting is not yet published in the documentation found.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Fabric DLP restrict access pricing additional action charge asset per day; site:azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/purview Fabric data loss prevention restrict access price. Read Purview billing models and Fabric DLP overview/configuration; no action-specific surcharge found.

claims.claim: Excluding workspaces changes the assets in the policy's scope.
claims.quote: The policy only applies to five of these Fabric workspaces. The asset count for this policy is 250.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal creation route reaches the restrict access section of a Fabric DLP rule.
claims.quote: The Define policy settings page appears. Choose Create or customize advanced DLP rules ... On the Customize advanced DLP rules page ... Select Create rule.
claims.fix: Use 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Assign admin units > Fabric and Power BI workspaces > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > Actions > Restrict access or encrypt the content in Microsoft 365 locations > Block users from receiving email, or accessing shared SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams files, and Power BI items' from https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/governance/data-loss-prevention-configure. Keep the existing note about naming the policy and passing admin units. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-use-policies-non-microsoft-cloud-apps for the opening 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy' navigation.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule with Name, Policy, ContentContainsSensitiveInformation containing Name, and BlockAccess $true creates a DLP rule that blocks matching content.
claims.quote: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name "SocialSecurityRule" -Policy "USFinancialChecks" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name="U.S. Social Security Number (SSN)"} -BlockAccess $True

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal path reaches Edit for Fabric workspace inclusions and exclusions.
claims.quote: Select Fabric and Power BI workspaces as the location for the DLP policy. ... To specify specific workspaces for inclusion or exclusion, select Edit.
claims.fix: Keep the path and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-use-policies-non-microsoft-cloud-apps, whose creation steps give 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy'; the cited Fabric configuration page supplies the subsequent Fabric-specific steps.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy with PowerBIDlpLocation All, PowerBIDlpLocationException workspace IDs and Mode Enable creates an enabled policy excluding those workspaces.
claims.quote: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name "PowerBIPolicy" -Comment "Primary policy" -PowerBIDlpLocation "All" -PowerBIDlpLocationException "workspaceID1","workspaceID2","workspaceID3" -Mode Enable
claims.fix: Append to controls[1].note: 'The PowerShell reference describes qualifying Power BI workspaces as hosted on Premium Gen2 capacities; the Fabric configuration page says Fabric or Premium capacities.' Keep both existing reference links and the test-tenant caveat.

claims.claim: After Custom policy, the admin names and describes the policy and selects Next.
claims.quote: Name the policy and provide a meaningful description. When done, select Next.

claims.claim: The admin passes Assign admin units with Next without assigning units.
claims.quote: Select Next when you get to the Assign admin units page. Admin units are not supported for DLP in Fabric and Power BI.
